title: Festival Passport
new_concept: Floats from festivals around the world roll past on the projector; the class guesses what is being celebrated from the food, music and clothes, then hears the story behind it, sees where it happens on the map, and joins in one song or move.
why: Wave 1. Repeats the live art-passport (world map, passport stamps) in K-2.

title: Bee Bot Garden
cluster_title: Coding a creature through a garden, K-2
new_concept: The class lays arrow cards to send a mail mouse across a snowy town grid; before it runs, kids trace the route with a finger and predict where it will stop, then run it and fix the card that sent it the wrong way.
why: Programs a creature through a garden like the live loop-garden and robot-dance; 'Bee-Bot' is a TTS product name.

title: Input-Output Machine
new_concept: A tablet, a game controller, a smart speaker and a microwave; the class sorts each part into 'takes in' or 'gives out', then predicts what the gadget does when one input is covered.
why: Same skill and setting (a desktop computer's parts) as the live computer-builder.

title: Design the Study
new_concept: Test whether energy drinks really speed up reaction times: choose random assignment, a control group, blinding and a placebo, and a skeptical journal editor shows how each missing piece lets a hidden variable fake the result. Surveys and sampling stay with poll-workshop.
why: Shares S-IC.B and the newsroom setting with the live poll-workshop, which already covers sampling, wording and bias.

title: Local Changemaker Planner
new_concept: Pick a local problem (a dangerous crosswalk, a closed library branch) and trace who actually decides it: which office, which meeting, when public comment opens; then draft the testimony or petition that reaches them.
why: Same town setting, the same community-project task and a near-identical title as the live community-project-planner.

title: Power Grid Tycoon
cluster_title: A city to run beside a live city tycoon
new_concept: Keep a city's lights on from the grid control room, mixing coal, gas, solar, wind and nuclear; balance cost, reliability and emissions through a heat wave and a still, cloudy week.
why: Manages a city like the live community-project-planner; the title is also the Power Grid board game.

title: Boundaries Builder
new_concept: Place short friendship and dating scenarios on a line from healthy to unhealthy; red-flag cards explain each placement, and a 'what you could say' card practices setting the boundary.
options: Move to the 6-8 nutrition gap: 'Day of Meals: Plan a day of meals and snacks around a busy schedule (practice, a test, a late night), then see how energy, focus and mood hold up and adjust the plan.'
why: Practices peer communication in scenarios like the live conflict-coach.

title: Compound Interest Garden
new_concept: Live a year of surprise costs (a flat tire, a cracked phone, a vet bill) with and without an emergency fund, then see what the fund grows to if it sits untouched for ten years.
why: Grows savings over decades like the live savings-plan and market-time-machine.

title: Roller Coaster Physics
new_concept: Design a zipline from a cliff platform to a far tree; with friction on, energy conservation decides whether the rider reaches the far platform and how hard the brake has to work.
why: A coaster track in grade 11 beside the live rollercoaster-polynomials, with a near-identical title.

title: Move Like Me
cluster_title: Copying moves on the board, K-2
new_concept: An animated dancer stretches, twists and bends at high, middle and low levels, then travels straight, curved and zigzag pathways; the class copies each one, then invents a pathway for the dancer to follow.
why: Copying moves from the board, like the live animal-moves and beat-buddies.

title: Two Sides Theater
cluster_title: The Three Little Pigs twice in grade 2
new_concept: Goldilocks and Baby Bear tell the same morning (beginning, middle and end) two ways; tap a character to hear the scene in their voice and see their thought bubble, then the class voices the next scene as the other character.
why: Uses the Three Little Pigs, the story of the live grade 2 three-pigs-lab.

title: Elevator Hundred
new_concept: Slide beads on a 100-bead string, ten at a time and one at a time, to solve 34 + 20 or 47 + 6, then write the slides as an equation.
why: An elevator in K-2 beside the live sound-elevator; a hundred-chart climb would repeat the live hundred-hop.

title: Text Feature Safari
new_concept: A plain page about ocean animals is hard to use; the class adds a heading, captions, labels and a glossary one at a time and sees which question each one helps answer faster.
why: A safari in K-2 beside the live line-safari and orchestra-zoo.

title: Book Detectives
new_concept: An author and an illustrator take turns showing their part of a picture book; the class decides which job made each part of the page (words or pictures) and names the book's main topic and two details that tell about it.
why: A detective case in K-2 beside the live resource-detective.

title: Market Day
new_concept: With five tokens, the class shops a weekend market as consumers; each stall sells a good or offers a service, every choice means giving something else up, and the stall owners explain what they made or did.
why: A second K-2 stall to run beside the live corner-store.

title: Bundle Bakery
new_concept: Pack the class's loose crayons into boxes of ten for every table; say how many boxes and loose crayons, then compare two classrooms' supplies with >, = and <.
why: A third K-2 shop beside the live corner-store, and a grade 1 bakery beside blend-bakery; a cookie conveyor would repeat make-ten-machine.

title: Pattern Block Pond
cluster_title: A pond twice in kindergarten math
new_concept: Snap pattern blocks together to fill a stained-glass window outline; the window glows when two triangles make a rhombus.
why: A pond scene in kindergarten math beside the live hundred-hop.

title: Shape Spy
new_concept: A teddy bear hides beside, above, behind or under 3D solids in a toy room; the class names the solid, says whether it is flat or solid, and calls the position word before the teacher lifts the cover.
why: Hunts 2D shapes like the live line-safari's shape-hunt mode and shape-talk.

title: Pizza Party
new_concept: Fold and cut paper shapes (squares, circles, rectangles) into halves and fourths for a class art project; uneven cuts leave a friend with a smaller piece, and the class spots which cuts are fair.
why: A third K-2 food tool beside the live hamburger-paragraph and lunch-tray-builder (load relief, not a 2 of 3 clash).

title: Retell Puppets
cluster_title: Retelling on a puppet stage, K-2
new_concept: A sleepy puppet friend asks to hear a short story again; learners retell the beginning, middle and end with sentence frames and picture prompts, answering 'what happened first? then what?', and the friend drifts off after a complete retell.
options: Merge into story-stage as an ELD sentence-frame mode (needs one tool serving two modules)
why: Matches story-stage on skill, action and setting, and shares its family.

title: Class Snack Vote
new_concept: A ball bounces for ten seconds; half the class tallies the bounces by hand while the computer counts them too; compare the totals and the mistakes, then use the computer's counts to pick the bounciest ball.
why: Runs the same class vote as class-poll (g1 math); its CS codes are unique, so the slot stays and the angle moves to the computer.

title: Pattern Finder
cluster_title: Teaching an AI from pictures, K-2
new_concept: Everyday scenes play out (a phone unlocking with a face, a map choosing a route, a toy that answers back); the class guesses which ones use AI, and the teacher reveals the pattern each one learned from.
why: With its action corrected it matches teach-the-robot on skill, action and setting.

title: Debate Prep Desk
new_concept: Pick a kid-relevant issue (a later school start?), write a claim, then choose which of eight facts actually support it; off-topic and weak facts bounce out, and the paragraph builds from the ones that hold.
why: Practices counterarguments, which W.6.1 does not ask for; grade 7 owns counterclaims.

title: Town Hall Debate
new_concept: A group-chat argument about a school rule gets rewritten for the school board: sort each message into your claim, an opposing claim or neither, then write a formal paragraph that names the strongest opposing claim fairly and shows exactly where the two part ways.
why: A third rebuttal tool in 6-8 and a third assembly beside agora-assembly and constitutional-convention; grade 8 adds distinguishing the opposing claim.

title: Fruit Sorter AI
new_concept: Choose which features (color, edge, shape, size) a classifier may use to sort leaves by tree; see which features separate them and which only add noise, then test it on leaves it has never seen.
why: Trains and tests a classifier like biased-bot one grade down; fruit also put it beside kitchen-lab.

title: Director's Chair
new_concept: Stage the same short scene as a Greek chorus, Noh, commedia, Elizabethan and modern realist production; compare what each tradition's staging rules make the audience notice.
why: Switching interpretations of a classic scene repeats globe-theatre-stage in 9-12.

title: Premise Inspector
new_concept: Lay out the Declaration's argument as premises and a conclusion, then test later responses (Seneca Falls, Douglass's Fifth of July speech, the Gettysburg Address) by which premise each accepts, stretches or rejects.
why: Reads founding documents beside later speeches, the same texts and move as founding-words-explorer.

title: Founding Words Explorer
new_concept: Read founding documents with plain-English layers and historical context; trace how each document's central ideas develop across its sections.
why: Cuts 'echoes in later speeches', which belongs to premise-inspector (RI.11-12.9).

title: Fossil Dig
new_concept: Match each fossil (a fish, a fern, a coral) to the place it lived, then piece together what this desert used to be and which animals could survive the change.
why: Reads layers and fossils for a past environment like canyon-reader one grade up.

title: Evidence Locker
new_concept: For each reason in an opinion paragraph, choose the quote that backs it and write the sentence that introduces it; a quote that only repeats the reason fades out.
why: Quotes text as proof in a detective setting, like inference-interrogation in the same band.

title: Polynomial Garden
new_concept: Set x = 10 and watch every polynomial become an ordinary number; multiplying polynomials turns into long multiplication without carrying, and like terms line up like place-value columns.
why: The same rectangle area model as algebra-tile-studio in grade 9, and one of eight 'Garden' titles.

title: Courtroom Statistics
why: Kept: 'the null is innocent until proven guilty' is the standard teaching frame; the alternative would repeat fair-dice-investigation. Call closed.

title: Fair Use Court
new_concept: Work as a reviewer for a student video site; weigh each upload (a meme, a remix, a class project) against the four fair use factors, then cite each source and choose a Creative Commons license for your own work.
why: One of four mock trials in 9-12.

title: Robber Baron or Captain?
new_concept: Place industrialists on a line from robber baron to captain of industry using evidence cards (wages, prices, philanthropy, monopolies); the class compares placements and argues the hardest cases.
why: One of four mock trials in 9-12; empire-debate is already the grade 11 debate.

title: Pattern Detective
new_concept: Color the multiplication table to make patterns pop (every even product, every multiple of 5, the square numbers), predict the next colored square and explain the rule in one sentence, then use a pattern to crack a two-step word problem.
why: One of four detective mysteries in 3-5.

title: Network Detective
new_concept: Families call the help desk because a device won't connect; ask the right questions (wired or wireless? signed in, or just not allowed?) and fix each one.
why: One of four detective mysteries in 3-5.

title: Shape Courtroom
new_concept: Shapes drop through a stack of sieves (four sides, parallel pairs, right angles, equal sides) and stop at the most specific name they earn; the class predicts where a square lands.
why: A second mock trial in grade 5 beside claim-court, and a repeat of shape-family-tree's square-or-rectangle argument.

title: pH Detective
options: Rename to Mystery Liquids, concept unchanged (recommended)
Move to the HS-PS3-4 gap: 'Even Out: Drop hot metal into cold water, mix hot and cold water, and predict the final temperature; watch energy flow until both sides match.' Needs a new module row.
why: One of four 9-12 mysteries and one of twelve 'Detective' titles; identifying unknowns by pH is real lab work, so the case frame stays.

title: Mad Libs Machine
why: Mad Libs is a Penguin Random House mark.

title: Food Web Jenga
why: Jenga is a Hasbro mark.

title: Battleship Grid
new_concept: Hide boats on the first quadrant and call coordinates to find a partner's; each miss tells you how far off you were.
why: Battleship is a Hasbro mark; distance feedback makes it more than the board game.

title: Rube Goldberg Workshop
why: The Rube Goldberg name is licensed by Rube Goldberg Inc.

title: Lemonade Monopoly
new_concept: The same phone-charger market runs twice, once with four competing makers and once after one buys out the rest; compare prices, choice and quality side by side, then see what regulators can do.
why: Uses the Monopoly name, echoes lemonade-stand, and shares a family and standard with the live concert-ticket-market.

title: Chain Reaction
new_concept: A picture story (a dropped ice cream, a missed bus) runs backward one step at a time; learners link each step with because, so or as a result to rewind it to the start.
why: A chain-reaction machine beside the science Contraption Workshop in 3-5.

title: Treasure Map Steps
new_concept: Two-step clues about what came in and went out of the lost and found each day ('14 mittens, 6 picked up, 5 more found') point to the box that holds the missing toy.
why: One of four treasure hunts in K-2; matches place-value-vault on action and setting.

title: Story Map Treasure
new_concept: Sew a story quilt one square at a time (beginning, problem, how the character feels, solution, lesson), choosing the picture that belongs in each square and retelling it aloud.
why: One of four treasure hunts in K-2.

title: Recipe Scaler
new_concept: Each costume for the school play takes 3/8 yard of fabric and 2/3 of a spool of ribbon; scale up for the whole cast and work out how many bolts and spools to buy, then add up the scraps left over.
why: One of three food shops and three measuring-cup tools in 3-5 math.

title: Pizza Shop Assembly Line
new_concept: Make paper airplanes alone, then on an assembly line with specialized jobs; productivity jumps, and the class sees how each worker depends on the others.
why: A food shop to run, beside grocery-run and recipe-scaler in 3-5.

title: Keyword Kitchen
new_concept: Cast a search with the keywords you choose and see what you catch; too broad pulls in junk and too narrow catches nothing.
why: A kitchen experiment beside kitchen-lab and fraction-kitchen in 3-5.

title: Pizza Physics
new_concept: Settle classic round-object arguments (one big trampoline or two small ones? a 26-inch bike wheel or a 20-inch?) by measuring circumference and area.
why: A kitchen experiment beside reaction-kitchen and the live smoothie-lab in 6-8.

title: Ice Cream Shop
new_concept: Design snow globes, cone-shaped tree ornaments and cylinder bases; volume decides how much water and glitter each needs and what each costs to make.
why: A second food shop to run in 6-8 math beside tax-and-tip and lemonade-stand.

title: Dance Floor Moves
new_concept: An L-shaped cargo tile must land exactly on its outline; slide, flip, turn and resize it in the fewest moves, then replay the route as a sequence of rules and decide which docks were congruent and which only similar.
why: Choreographs to music on a stage like choreography-board in 6-8.

title: Transformation Golf
new_concept: Each level shows a shape and its twin; map one onto the other with the fewest rigid motions, then write the sequence as the proof that they are congruent.
why: A second golf course in 9-12 math beside equation-golf; 'Transformation Golf' is also a Desmos activity.

title: Choreography Board
new_concept: Build a dance on a timeline of movement phrases (counts, levels, dynamics), then revise it; formations show in a side view as the phrases play to music.
why: Places performers on a top-down stage like stage-blocker in 6-8.

title: Space Cargo
new_concept: Slide stones of different masses with different pushes along the ice; F = ma predicts where each one stops, and sweeping changes the friction.
why: One of three space simulators in 9-12 (with launch-pad, wave 1, and orbit-lab).

title: Inquiry Planner
new_concept: Start from a broad interest and narrow it into a researchable question; the tool tests each draft (too broad, too narrow, already answered) and maps what you would need to find out.
why: A business tycoon beside ad-agency and startup-tycoon, and a second research planner beside research-notebook.

title: Island Economy
new_concept: Manage a lake town's fish, forest and water over generations, through good years and flood years; sustainable use keeps the town going and overuse brings collapse.
why: One of four islands in 9-12; matches trade-island on action and setting.

title: Build a Government
new_concept: Design a government for a newly formed country; pick a system, write its powers, and test it against crises (a disputed election, a famine, a leader who won't leave).
why: One of four islands in 9-12.

title: Argument Frames Pro
cluster_title: Debates in 9-12 and the two "Pro" titles
why: Title differs by one word from argument-builder-pro (9-12); the ELD scaffolds already make the tool different.

title: Scam Shield
cluster_title: Scams, insurance and a year of surprises, 9-12
new_concept: Compare three insurance quotes side by side; a slider trades the monthly premium against the deductible, and a claim calculator shows who pays what for a stolen bike or a fender bender. A last round sorts real insurer messages from fake 'claim refund' texts.
why: An escape room on scams beside capture-the-flag; a 'year of surprises' would repeat Rainy Day Fund.

title: Flowchart Factory
why: A second 'Factory' title in 6-8 beside function-machine-factory; the factory is only in the title, so the concept stands.

title: Essay Architect
new_concept: Paragraphs are train cars; each coupling is a transition, and a weak one lets the cars drift apart until the order and the links make sense.
why: A construction metaphor beside story-building-blocks and blueprint-builder in 3-5 ELA.

title: Blueprint Builder
new_concept: One set of facts about a hurricane appears as a timeline, a cause-and-effect chain and a problem-and-solution article; students name each structure and say which question each version answers best.
why: A third construction metaphor in 3-5 ELA, a near-identical title to blueprint-studio, and a writing task on a reading standard (RI.4.5).

title: Source Sorter
new_concept: Give each source a quick credibility check, then practice quoting it and paraphrasing it; the tool flags paraphrases that copy too closely and builds the citation for each version.
why: Credibility is all of fake-or-fact-lab; source-sorter keeps one check (W.6.8 asks for it) and leads with quoting, paraphrasing and citing.

title: Snack Scale
new_concept: Line up two rows of snacks one to one; the leftovers show which group has more, and the class says the numbers before the teacher matches them up.
why: Predict-then-reveal on a tipping scale, the same game as who-wins in kindergarten math.

title: Skate Park Energy
cluster_title: Slopes for a rider in grade 8
new_concept: Pull a playground swing back and let go; kinetic and potential energy trade places in a live bar chart, and a longer pull or a heavier rider changes the totals.
why: Designs a slope for a rider like ski-slope-designer in grade 8; 'Energy Skate Park' is also a PhET simulation.

title: Cone Slicer
new_concept: Drag a point so its distances to two foci (or to a focus and a line) follow one rule, and watch an ellipse, a hyperbola or a parabola appear; then find each one's equation.
why: One of three slice-or-spin-a-solid explorers in 9-12 math (with slice-it and solid-spinner).

title: Meal and Move Planner
new_concept: Plan a week of meals around your training days; the tool tracks energy in and out, flags gaps and extremes, and shows how the plan holds up on a game day.
why: Plans workouts like fitness-program-designer in 9-12 health; FITT programming stays with that tool.

title: Depth Detective
why: One of twelve 'Detective' titles.

title: Root Detective Cards
why: One of twelve 'Detective' titles.

title: Screen Time Detective
why: One of twelve 'Detective' titles.

title: Data Detective
why: One of twelve 'Detective' titles; echoes the CS 6-8 module 'Data Detectives'.

title: Unit Detective
why: One of twelve 'Detective' titles.

title: Watershed Detective
why: One of twelve 'Detective' titles.

title: Word Zoo
why: 'Zoo' beside the live orchestra-zoo in K-2; the concept already sorts words into habitats.

title: Story Dress-Up
why: 'Story' beside story-stage and my-story-strip in K-2.

title: Particle Zoom
why: A zoom explorer with 'Zoom' in the title beside powers-of-ten-zoom in grade 5.

title: Summary Scaffold
why: Same skill and a one-word title difference from summary-squeeze in 6-8.

title: Counterclaim Ping-Pong
options: Rename to Counterclaim Rally ('Ping-Pong' is a registered mark for table tennis gear)
why: Low title caution only; the tool stays the grade 7 counterclaim tool.

title: Sentence Remixer
why: Spec check: lead with style and pronouns (L.6.3, L.6.1); clause function belongs to sentence-diagram-builder (L.7.1).

title: Song Form Builder
why: Spec check: AB and ABA forms also appear in dance-pattern-puzzle (3-5); keep the music on form and the dance on movement.

title: Speedometer
why: Spec check: lead with the derivative as rate; graph matching belongs to the live motion-graph-match.

title: Inbox Simulator
why: Spec check: stay on email and register; job interviews belong to interview-simulator.

title: Prototype Lab
why: Spec check: iterate one product; breaking down a global problem belongs to design-challenge-studio.

title: Population Dashboard
options: Keep as written (recommended once energy-accountant takes HS-LS2-5, W3)

Move to the HS-ESS2-7 gap: 'Living Planet: Scrub through four billion years and watch life and Earth change each other: microbes fill the air with oxygen, plants build soil, reefs build coastlines.' Needs a new module row and leaves science-12-population-and-resources without a tool.
why: One of 12 data-format tools in 9-12; its standards are also on island-economy and carrying-capacity.

title: Voice Switcher
options: Keep (recommended): news headlines that hide who is to blame are the strongest passive-voice hook in the catalog
Reshape to Play-by-Play Voice: sports commentary switching between active and passive voice
why: One of five newsroom settings in 6-8; the rule hit was between two other newsroom tools.

title: Make Ten Machine
why: Wave 1. Owns the conveyor and tens-packing picture in K-2 math; ten-frame-factory is retitled and bundle-bakery leaves the conveyor (Crayon Boxes).

title: Ten Frame Factory
why: Factory title beside make-ten-machine's conveyor (wave 1); the concept has no factory in it.

title: Town Planner: Disaster Ready
why: Wave 1. Owns hazards, floods and dams in grade 4; settle-the-valley is trimmed to leave them out.

title: Settle the Valley
new_concept: Settle a valley: choose where farms, homes and roads go and see how the land and the people change each other, from cleared forests and worn-out soil to new trails and trade.
why: Builds a settlement with dams and floods like town-planner-disaster-ready (wave 1) in grade 4.

title: Energy Accountant
options: Add HS-LS2-5 (and optionally HS-LS2-3) to its module before the wave 1 spec (recommended)
Leave it and give HS-LS2-5 its own tool later (a new module row; an earlier draft re-pointed population-dashboard there as 'Carbon Relay')
why: Wave 1. Its carbon and energy ledger already models photosynthesis and respiration; HS-LS2-5 is the carbon cycle across the spheres and has no module.
